_about: A relevance benchmark for Firmo's search.
Each case is a topic a student might actually type, paired with papers a
human judged squarely on-topic for it. Those papers are the ground truth: a
run scores by how many of them Firmo surfaces, and how high.
Every DOI here was resolved against CrossRef before being added. That check
matters more than it sounds: a first draft of this file was written from
memory and a third of the DOIs were wrong, one of them pointing at an
entirely different paper. A benchmark with bad ground truth is worse than no
benchmark, because it reports confident nonsense. Verify before adding.
Fields:
must_find         DOIs of papers a good search has to return.
must_find_titles  Titles, for papers with no CrossRef DOI. arXiv registers
with DataCite, so an arXiv-only paper can never be matched
by DOI and would otherwise be scored as a permanent miss.
off_topic_terms   Words that signal the wrong sense of an ambiguous query.
Counted separately because that failure ('armed conflict'
for 'high-conflict divorce') is the one semantic ranking
was introduced to fix.
This set is small and honest about it: a regression net that catches a
ranking change quietly breaking humanities coverage, not a published
benchmark. Grow it whenever a real query returns something wrong.

cases.query: how high conflict divorce affects children
how did the printing press change literacy in europe
social media use and adolescent mental health
does raising the minimum wage cause unemployment
